selection_rationale: CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II continuation workload (no GPU needed). Plan target was AMD EPYC 7B13 64-core at $0.2382/hr (matching t0081's offer 31639237 / machine 55891 in Norway). That exact offer is unavailable today. Of all current >=99% reliable offers under $0.30/hr with >=64 GB RAM and >=36 effective cores, the only candidate is Xeon E5-2690 v2 (Ivy Bridge 2013 uArch) at $0.0947/hr -- ~2-3x slower per-core than EPYC Zen 3, which would push wall-clock and cost-per-cell well beyond t0081's measured envelope and risk substrate-consistency drift in the smoke gate. Of all EPYC offers with 36+ cores and >=64 GB RAM, the cheapest is offer 24887414 at $0.3209/hr: AMD EPYC 7B13 64-Core Processor (SAME silicon family as t0081's machine 55891), 42.67 effective cores in this fractional rental, 332 GB host RAM advertised (verified 995 GB total, 972 GB available inside container), 25 GB container disk allocated, Debian 12 bookworm container (host kernel Ubuntu 22.04), 0.9992 reliability, ~25-day duration remaining, Texas US (machine_id 27647, public IP 38.247.78.2). EPYC 7B13 microarchitecture identity guarantees the smoke gate's substrate-consistency check will hold within tolerances (DSI +/- 0.05, PD +/- 1.0 Hz). Cost projection: at 42.67/64 = 1.50x the per-cell wall-clock of t0081's 64-core run -> 6.0-13.4 h instance lifetime for 5-10 additional generations. Cost worst case: 13.4 h * $0.3209/hr = $4.30, plus ~$0.16 provisioning/setup overhead = $4.46, comfortably under the $5.00 hard cap configured by the cost-cap watchdog. Cost best case: 6.0 h * $0.3209 = $1.93. Selected over the $0.5608/hr 64-core EPYC 7B13 offer 36069152 (Quebec, reliability only 0.9940) because that rate would push 10-gen worst case to $5.97 (over the $5.00 cap). Selected over the AMD Threadripper PRO 5995WX 64-core at $0.1747/hr (offer 35336703) because its 63 GB cpu_ram falls below the 64 GB minimum stated in the task brief, and the substrate-consistency risk of changing CPU family (Threadripper vs EPYC, both Zen 3 but different microcode/timing) is unwarranted when an EPYC option exists within budget. Acknowledged risk: per-cell wall-clock scales as 64/43 ~= 1.5x, so the run is more likely to hit the cost-cap watchdog or the gen-17 hard cap before the HV-plateau watchdog fires; this is a documented Risks & Fallbacks table entry in plan.md and is acceptable per the task's 'acceptable negative' pass criterion (HV > 16.33 with plateau detected even with zero additional joint-pass cells).
